territory: Cross-cutting lens: database connection budget and pgbouncer/Supavisor compatibility — pool arithmetic from installed driver sources, every $transaction and raw-SQL call site, DIRECT_URL isolation, session-callback cost, per-pageview connection dwell, build-time DB usage, and the chaos behavior when the database degrades.

findings.title: Place gazetteer search does a full 234,934-row sequential scan on every keystroke of 4+ characters: the altNames ILIKE arm in an OR defeats both expression indexes, and ~15-25 members typing in the onboarding city picker saturate the Supavisor pooler for the whole site
findings.expected: Type-ahead city search stays on the two `lower(...) text_pattern_ops` expression indexes at every query length, so each keystroke costs single-digit milliseconds and the shared pooler never notices it.
findings.actual: For queries of 4+ characters (i.e. most of every city name typed: "chen", "chenn", "chennai") the WHERE clause becomes `indexable-arm OR indexable-arm OR altNames ILIKE '%q%'`. Postgres can only use a BitmapOr when EVERY arm of an OR is indexable; `"altNames"` has no index of any kind (schema.prisma:636 is a bare `String?`, no migration creates one — verified across all of prisma/migrations-manual/), so the planner falls back to a sequential scan of the full 234,934-row Place table, evaluating `lower()` twice plus an ILIKE over a long comma-joined text column per row, per keystroke, per member.
findings.evidence: src/app/api/places/search/route.ts:99-109: `const altNamesClause = raw.length >= 4 ? Prisma.sql`OR "altNames" ILIKE ${containsPattern} ESCAPE '\\'` : Prisma.empty;` folded into `WHERE lower("asciiName") LIKE lower(${prefixPattern}) ESCAPE '\\' OR lower("name") LIKE lower(${prefixPattern}) ESCAPE '\\' ${altNamesClause}`. The only indexes on Place are `CREATE INDEX ... ON "Place" (lower("asciiName") text_pattern_ops)` and the same for name (2026-07-18-round6.sql:30-31) — grep for `pg_trgm|GIN|altNames` across prisma/migrations-manual/*.sql finds no altNames index. The route's own comment admits the arm "degrades to a sequential scan" but treats the 4-char gate as the mitigation; 4+ chars is the COMMON case for a real city name, not the rare one. The arithmetic: Supabase Free plan (docs/OPERATIONS.md:57 "Supabase's free plan has no automatic backups") means Nano compute with Supavisor's default transaction-mode pool_size of ~15 server connections. A 234k-row seq scan with per-row lower()+ILIKE on shared nano CPU is realistically 80-200ms. Ceiling = 15 slots / 0.15s ≈ 100 scans/s. A member typing fires ~3 requests/s (the rate limit at line 84 deliberately allows 120/min); so ~15-25 members simultaneously typing in the LocationPicker — exactly the launch-day onboarding shape, and src/lib/email-queue.ts:18-20 records the owner "expects more than 100 signups on the first day" — occupies every server connection, and EVERY other query in the app (feed, login, notification counts) queues behind the scans at the pooler. Combined with the missing timeouts (next finding) the queue manifests as site-wide hangs, not errors.
findings.fixDirection: Two independent fixes, either sufficient: (1) add `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm; CREATE INDEX ON "Place" USING gin ("altNames" gin_trgm_ops);` in a dated migrations-manual file and keep the query as-is (BitmapOr then works for all three arms); or (2) restructure so the OR never mixes indexable and non-indexable arms — run the two prefix arms first (indexed), and only if they return fewer than LIMIT 8 rows run the altNames contains query as a separate statement (or UNION ALL with per-arm LIMIT). Option 2 also cuts the common-case cost to zero extra. Keep the existing ORDER BY semantics (exact match, then own-name prefix, then population).
findings.gateOrTest: After the fix, run `EXPLAIN SELECT id FROM "Place" WHERE lower("asciiName") LIKE 'chen%' OR lower("name") LIKE 'chen%' OR "altNames" ILIKE '%chen%'` via scripts/dev/run-sql.mjs and pin that the plan contains no `Seq Scan on "Place"`; add that EXPLAIN assertion as a script check so a future query edit cannot silently regress it.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: run the EXPLAIN above through scripts/dev/run-sql.mjs (SELECT-only) and observe `Seq Scan on Place` with a 4+ char pattern vs `BitmapOr` with a 3-char pattern; optionally time 20 parallel curl requests to /api/places/search?q=chennai against the dev server and watch other routes' latency climb.

findings.title: Supabase Free plan cannot carry the 2,000-member ceiling: database egress alone lands multiples over the 5GB/month cap, on top of the already-documented no-backups and Nano-compute constraints
findings.expected: The database plan has quota headroom for the stated 2,000-user maximum: query-result egress, compute, and connection caps all clear the projected load.
findings.actual: The project is on the Supabase Free plan (docs/OPERATIONS.md:57 states it outright), whose bundled egress is 5GB/month across database + storage. Every authenticated pageview moves roughly 20-60KB of query results out of Supabase (feed/letters post bodies, directory rows, plus the ~13-16 statements per pageview the (main) layout and drain pass run — see coverage notes). At even a conservative 400 daily-active members x 20 pageviews x 30KB, that is ~240MB/day ≈ 7GB/month; at the owner's 2,000-member ceiling with launch-week engagement it is 20-90GB/month. Past the cap Supabase issues over-usage warnings and can restrict the project — i.e. the site degrades precisely when it succeeds. Free also pins Nano compute, which is the denominator in the gazetteer-scan finding, and OPERATIONS.md already documents the no-backup consequence separately.
findings.evidence: docs/OPERATIONS.md:57: "Supabase's free plan has **no automatic backups and no point-in-time recovery**" — the plan is Free, stated in the repo's own ops doc. Per-pageview volume is code-verified: src/app/(main)/layout.tsx:35-52 runs `prisma.notification.count`, `advanceDueCatchups(session.user.id)` (a CatchupEdition findMany minimum), `touchLastSeen` (Visit upsert + User updateMany), plus the page's own list queries, plus the `after(drainMailQueue)` pass (5 more statements); feed/letters pages then transfer full post/letter text columns per row. The 5GB/month Free-tier egress figure is a Supabase plan quota, external to the repo — hence status suspected — but the multiplication needs only the repo-side facts above to show the cap is exceeded at any realistic fraction of 2,000 members. R2 already carries image bytes (zero egress), so this is text/query egress alone.
findings.fixDirection: This is an ops decision for the owner, pre-launch: upgrade the Supabase project to Pro ($25/mo, 250GB egress, real backups, Micro+ compute) before public release — it simultaneously retires this finding, doubles down on the backup gap OPERATIONS.md already flags, and raises the compute floor under the gazetteer-scan finding. Secondary code lever if egress must shrink: trim over-fetching in list views (select only the columns rendered) — but the plan upgrade is the real fix.
findings.gateOrTest: Ops checklist item, not a code gate: after upgrade, verify plan and compute tier in the Supabase dashboard; optionally record the decision in docs/OPERATIONS.md next to the backup paragraph.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: Supabase dashboard usage page shows current egress run-rate; multiply by the member-growth factor. No app interaction needed.

findings.title: No timeout at any layer for ordinary queries: pool checkout queues forever (pg default), no connect/statement/query timeout is configured, so a slow or wedged database turns into multi-minute blank-page hangs and platform 504s instead of the app's error page — and each hung request holds pool and concurrency slots, compounding the incident
findings.expected: When the database is slow, saturated, or a query wedges, a member's request fails fast into src/app/error.tsx ("something went wrong, retry") within a few seconds, and the stuck request releases its connection so the incident does not snowball.
findings.actual: The adapter is constructed as `new PrismaPg({ connectionString })` (src/lib/prisma.ts:16) — no `connectionTimeoutMillis`, no `statement_timeout`, no `query_timeout`, no `max`. The installed pg-pool (node_modules/pg-pool/index.js) defaults `connectionTimeoutMillis` to unset, and its connect() path at lines 205-207 reads `if (!this.options.connectionTimeoutMillis) { this._pendingQueue.push(new PendingItem(response.callback)); return result; }` — the checkout waits in the pending queue with NO timer, forever. The (main) layout awaits its Promise.all BEFORE returning any JSX, above every loading.tsx boundary, so a hung checkout or hung statement means the member sees a blank page (not even the shimmer) until Vercel kills the function at the plan's max duration (minutes under Fluid compute) and returns a bare platform 504 — never the app's error.tsx. Meanwhile that request holds its Fluid concurrency slot and any already-checked-out connections, so under a DB brown-out the backlog compounds. Only interactive transactions have a bound (Prisma JS runtime defaults verified in node_modules/@prisma/client/runtime/client.js: `maxWait??2e3, timeout: ...??5e3`); the ~99% of traffic that is plain queries has none. Note the fast-failure path DOES work when the DB refuses connections outright (ECONNREFUSED -> DriverAdapterError -> error.tsx); it is specifically slowness/saturation that hangs.
findings.evidence: src/lib/prisma.ts:16: `const adapter = new PrismaPg({ connectionString });` — the config object is passed verbatim to `new pg.Pool(config)` (node_modules/@prisma/adapter-pg/dist/index.js:779-788). pg-pool defaults verified in node_modules/pg-pool/index.js: line 89 `this.options.max = this.options.max || this.options.poolSize || 10`, line 99 `this.options.idleTimeoutMillis = 10000`, lines 205-207 queue-without-timer as quoted above. src/app/(main)/layout.tsx:35 `const [unreadCount, mailState] = await Promise.all([...])` sits above the per-page loading.tsx boundaries, so its hang blanks the whole response.
findings.fixDirection: Pass explicit limits into the one PrismaPg construction site: `new PrismaPg({ connectionString, connectionTimeoutMillis: 5_000, statement_timeout: 15_000, query_timeout: 20_000 })` (pg forwards statement_timeout per-connection and enforces query_timeout client-side; both are pgbouncer-transaction-mode safe because pg applies statement_timeout via the startup/SET on the checked-out client per query — verify with one EXPLAIN-style smoke test through the 6543 pooler, and if SET-based statement_timeout proves unreliable through Supavisor, keep query_timeout + connectionTimeoutMillis, which are purely client-side). With a checkout timeout, exhaustion surfaces as `Error('timeout exceeded when trying to connect')` -> DriverAdapterError -> the server component throws -> src/app/error.tsx renders — the actionable path. Consider `max` left at 10 (the arithmetic in this audit shows 10/instance is ample).
findings.gateOrTest: A unit test in the security-regressions style that imports src/lib/prisma.ts's adapter options (export the options object) and asserts connectionTimeoutMillis/query_timeout are set, so a future refactor cannot silently drop them.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would require degrading the shared production database, which is off the table). The pg-pool queue-without-timer lines plus the layout's await placement are sufficient.

findings.title: Layout render blocks on an untimed Resend network call for unconfirmed members: a Resend brown-out (accepting connections but not answering) hangs every page view of every unconfirmed member for minutes, and the 2-minute stale-claim recycler makes it recur
findings.expected: The verification banner's self-heal ("send the queued row before answering") costs one bounded network call: if Resend does not answer within a few seconds, the layout renders with state "imminent" and the member gets their page.
findings.actual: src/app/(main)/layout.tsx:44-46 awaits `verificationMailState(session.user.id)` inside the render-blocking Promise.all for every member with `emailConfirmed` false. email-queue.ts:597-599: `if (row.status === "queued") { const outcome = await claimAndSend(row); ... }` — claimAndSend calls `sendMail`, and email.ts:181 `await api.emails.send({...})` has no AbortSignal, no timeout, no race. The Resend SDK's underlying undici fetch waits up to the default headers timeout (~300s). So when Resend is slow-but-up: the member's page render hangs behind the send; the row was already flipped to "sending" by the claim, so concurrent views take the fast `imminent` path for 2 minutes — then STALE_CLAIM_MS (email-queue.ts:101, `2 * 60_000`) recycles it to "queued" and the NEXT page view hangs again. Every unconfirmed member with a pending verify row loops through hang -> 2min grace -> hang for the duration of the provider incident. This is exactly taxonomy 6k "email provider down mid-signup", and signup week is when the maximum number of members are unconfirmed. The design intent ("Cost: one Resend call inside one page load, once" — email-queue.ts:561-562) assumed the call is bounded; it is not.
findings.evidence: email.ts:181-187: `const { data, error } = await api.emails.send({ from: FROM, to: opts.to, subject: opts.subject, html: opts.html, text: opts.text });` — no signal/timeout anywhere in the file (grep for `timeout|AbortSignal|signal` matches nothing). Contrast turnstile.ts:98 which does exactly the right thing for the same class of call: `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000)`. layout.tsx:44-46: `session.user.emailConfirmed ? Promise.resolve(null) : verificationMailState(session.user.id)` inside the awaited Promise.all.
findings.fixDirection: Bound sendMail the way turnstile is bounded: wrap the Resend call in `Promise.race` with a 5-8s timer (or pass fetch options if the SDK version supports a signal), returning `{ ok: false, error: "timeout" }` so claimAndSend's existing requeue path handles it. Independently, consider moving the layout's self-heal send behind `after()` (report the pre-send state synchronously as "imminent", repair post-response) so the render path never contains a mail-provider round trip at all — the banner's honesty invariant survives because the very next view reads the repaired row.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test for sendMail with an injected hanging fetch/SDK double asserting it settles within N seconds with ok:false; the existing email-flow unit tests are the natural home.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only in production terms; locally provable by pointing RESEND_API_KEY at a black-holing mock (dev-only env) and loading a page as an unconfirmed user — but the quoted code suffices.

findings.title: Collection upload fallback path dies at Vercel's 4.5MB request-body cap for any photo between 4.5MB and the advertised 20MB limit, with only a vague toast — and the fallback is the path every member is on while the R2 bucket CORS rule remains unconfigured
findings.expected: A member contributing a 12MB phone photo either uploads it via the presigned direct PUT (bytes never touch Vercel) or, on the fallback path, gets the friendly "over the 20MB limit"-style message the action was built to give.
findings.actual: contributePhoto is a Server Action accepting `formData.get("file")` up to `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = 20MB` (upload-shared.ts:9), and next.config.ts raises the Next-level caps to 25mb (serverActions.bodySizeLimit and proxyClientMaxBodySize). But Vercel's platform caps serverless request bodies at 4.5MB regardless of framework config, returning a 413 FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE before the action executes — the 25mb settings only govern local/self-hosted. The dialog knows this and prefers the presigned path (contribute-dialog.tsx:119-125: "Vercel's ~4.5MB request cap never sees the bytes"), but when `directUploadPut` returns null (its documented cases: "local dev without R2, or an origin the bucket's CORS rule does not name") it silently falls back to the Server Action (line 144). Project memory records the bucket CORS configuration as blocked on an admin-scoped token — if that is still true in production, EVERY member is on the fallback, and every photo over ~4.5MB fails with the generic catch toast ("The photo may be too large, or the connection dropped"), which matches the owner's previously reported "fails maybe 1-in-6" symptom. Modern phone photos are routinely 5-12MB.
findings.evidence: collection/actions.ts:131-132: `if (file.size > MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES) { return { error: \`Photo is over the 20MB limit...\` }; }` — a check that can never run on Vercel for the 4.5-20MB range because the platform rejects the body first. next.config.ts:111-122 raises only Next's own limits. contribute-dialog.tsx:126-144: `if (staged) { result = await contributePhotoDirect({...}) } else { const fd = new FormData(); fd.set("file", file); ... result = await contributePhoto(fd); }` — the >4.5MB fallback path is reachable whenever presign is unavailable, and its failure surfaces as the generic error at lines 149-157.
findings.fixDirection: Two-part: (1) operational — finish the R2 bucket CORS rule (the known blocked task) so the direct path actually works from the production origin; verify with a >5MB upload from a phone. (2) code — in the fallback branch, check `file.size` CLIENT-side against ~4MB before building the FormData and show a specific message ("this photo is too large to send the slow way; try again shortly / resize"), so the platform 413 is never the member's first signal. Optionally detect the 413 (the thrown action error) and name the size cause explicitly.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright spec (after live confirmation, per house rules) uploading a 6MB fixture through the dialog against a preview deployment: asserts either direct-path success or the specific size message — never the generic connection toast.
findings.reproPlan: Live, safe on the real app with a test account: open the Collection contribute dialog on production with DevTools network tab, attempt an ~8MB JPG; observe whether the PUT goes to R2 (CORS fixed) or a POST to the page returns 413 (fallback + cap). No data is written on the failing path.

findings.title: Nine fire-and-forget database writes rely on post-response execution without after()/waitUntil, so on serverless they are stochastically frozen mid-flight: telemetry rows (SearchLog, ContentView, LoginAttempt) and the AuthToken sweep silently under-record
findings.expected: "Not awaited so it never blocks" writes still eventually commit — the mental model in the comments (e.g. auth-tokens.ts:105 "a slow delete never holds up the mail") is background execution.
findings.actual: On Vercel, once the response completes, execution not registered via after()/waitUntil may be frozen; a `void somePrismaCall()` immediately before `return NextResponse.json(...)` (places/users search route handlers) has essentially zero guaranteed runway, and the in-render `void recordView(...)`/`void logSearch(...)` calls in four pages only survive if the remaining render outlasts their 1-3 round trips. The codebase already knows the correct tool — the layout wraps drainMailQueue in `after()` (layout.tsx:63) precisely because "it must run AFTER the response has been streamed" — but these nine sites do not use it. Consequences are bounded and silent by design: lost SearchLog rows (the owner's "most common searches" answer skews), lost ContentView increments (profile/letter view counts under-read), lost LoginAttempt rows (the admin analytics login-health view undercounts, including the failure reasons it exists to surface), and an AuthToken expiry sweep that fires less often than intended (table growth only — the weekly-past-expiry rows are also cleared by consumption paths). All are telemetry/cleanup; none corrupts member-facing state, hence Low — but it is the taxonomy's missing-await row and the comments show the survivability assumption is wrong, so it should be a deliberate decision rather than an accident.
findings.evidence: places/search/route.ts:127-133: `void logSearch({ scope: "places", ... }); return NextResponse.json(results);` — response returns with up to three queries (findFirst, update/create) un-started or in flight (search-log.ts:50-79). login-attempt.ts:46: `void prisma.loginAttempt` fire-and-forget in the authorize() path, where the sibling rate-limit spend at auth.ts:99-100 is explicitly awaited "so a serverless instance cannot freeze before the count lands" — the same reasoning applies to the row this one drops. auth-tokens.ts:107-110: `void prisma.authToken.deleteMany({ where: { expiresAt: { lt: ... } } })` immediately before `return { ok: true, token: raw, expiresAt };`.
findings.fixDirection: Mechanical: wrap each call site in `after(() => ...)` (the scheduleDrain helper in email-queue.ts:364-377 already shows the try-after-catch-run-inline pattern that also keeps scripts/tests working). Route handlers are the priority (zero runway); the in-render page calls and the auth-tokens sweep can follow the same pattern for consistency.
findings.gateOrTest: Grep-style regression check (same family as the lab-registry audit): no `void prisma.` / `void logSearch(` / `void recordView(` outside an after() wrapper; or simply convert all nine and let review pin it.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only; stochastic loss is not deterministically reproducible, which is exactly the problem.

verifiedClean: 6d SET/advisory-locks/LISTEN-NOTIFY through the transaction pooler: CLEAN — grep across src/ runtime code finds zero `SET`, `pg_advisory*`, `LISTEN`, `NOTIFY`, `set_config`, or `PREPARE` in any $queryRaw/$executeRaw; the only SET the driver ever issues is `SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL` INSIDE an open transaction (adapter dist index.js:731-737), which is transaction-scoped and Supavisor-safe.

6d prepared-statement pgbouncer hazard: CLEAN — the adapter sends every statement with `name: this.pgOptions?.statementNameGenerator?.(query)` (adapter dist index.js:656) and no statementNameGenerator is configured, so all statements are UNNAMED extended-protocol one-shots, fully compatible with transaction pooling; the `?pgbouncer=true` URL param is a legacy Prisma-engine flag node-pg simply ignores (harmless).

6d interactive $transaction holding network calls (the designated Critical-if-found): CLEAN — all 8 interactive sites read in full (catchups/actions.ts:326,441,856,911,1048; lib/catchups.ts:794 applyEditionAction, :917 openNextRoundIfDue; onboarding/actions.ts:78) contain ONLY DB statements (CAS updateMany + notification createMany builders in catchups-notify.ts, which is pure prisma), no R2/Resend/fetch; all are small and CAS-guarded, well inside the verified Prisma JS-runtime defaults maxWait=2s/timeout=5s (`maxWait??2e3,timeout:...??5e3` in @prisma/client/runtime/client.js).

6d batch $transaction sites: CLEAN by construction (arrays of PrismaPromises cannot interleave network work) — all 8 sites read: messages/actions.ts:137,183; admin/people/actions.ts:150 (updateUserPlaces, ≤32 stmts), :290 (merge, admin-only); settings/actions.ts:162; admin-threads-server.ts:67; account-purge.ts:99; auth-tokens.ts:91.
DIRECT_URL never read at runtime: CLEAN — exhaustive grep: only prisma.config.ts:26 (CLI) and scripts/* (dev/ops/qa tooling) reference it; zero hits under src/.

Build-time DB connections during static generation: CLEAN — the only statically-prerenderable pages (landing page.tsx, (policies), manifest.ts, (auth) forms) import no prisma; every prisma-importing page (including /lab, which reads LabRoomState) also calls auth()/headers() and is therefore request-time dynamic; module-scope client creation in src/lib/prisma.ts:99 constructs pg.Pool lazily (no connection until first query), so `next build` opens no DB connections.

Session-callback cost: CLEAN at this scale — auth.ts:245 does one primary-key `user.findUnique` per request, wrapped in React cache() at auth.ts:396 so layout+page+actions in one request collapse to one read; select list is 13 scalar columns, no relations.

Second-PrismaClient leak: CLEAN — only two construction sites in src/ (lib/prisma.ts singleton; api/demo/reset/route.ts per-call client that is demo-only, gated by IS_DEMO 404, and `$disconnect()`ed in finally).

Idle-connection error crash: CLEAN — the adapter attaches an 'error' listener to the pool (adapter dist index.js:789-793), so Supavisor closing idle clients (10s pg idle timeout churn) emits a handled event, not an uncaught-exception process crash.

Hot per-pageview query index coverage: CLEAN — Notification @@index([userId, read]) covers the layout count; OutboundEmail @@index([status, priority, createdAt]) covers the drain findFirst and reclaim, @@index([sentAt]) the budget count, @@index([userId, kind, status]) the enqueue fold; CatchupEdition @@index([status, publishAt]) covers advanceDueCatchups; Visit upsert is by primary key; User.lastSeenAt updateMany is by primary key.
6k Turnstile unreachable: CLEAN — turnstile.ts:98 `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` with documented fail-open and a loud production log for the missing-key case; sign-in cannot hang on Cloudflare.
proxy.ts per-request work: CLEAN — no DB, no fetch; header/cookie work only, so the edge layer adds zero connection load.

Cron overlap on the connection budget: CLEAN — catchups/tick delegates to the idempotent, CAS-guarded advanceDueCatchups (double-fire converges, each transition is one short tx); retention sweep is sequential deleteManys plus per-account purge whose report-clear+user-delete ride one batch tx with R2 deletes strictly AFTER commit (account-purge.ts:99-112) — no tx spans a network call.

Per-instance pool arithmetic at 2,000 users: CLEAN with ~100x headroom on connection COUNTS (full table in coverage notes) — the binding constraint is slow-query time (reported as the gazetteer finding), not connection count.
coverageNotes: READ WHOLE: src/lib/prisma.ts, auth.ts, rate-limit.ts, email-queue.ts, email.ts, last-seen.ts, search-log.ts, content-view.ts, retention.ts, account-purge.ts, catchups-notify.ts, (main)/layout.tsx, api/demo/reset, api/catchups/tick, api/retention/sweep, api/places/search, directory/where.ts, collection/actions.ts (upload half), collection contribute-dialog (submit path), turnstile.ts (verify half), auth-tokens.ts (mint), next.config.ts, vercel.json, prisma.config.ts. READ TARGETED: all 16 $transaction sites in full; lib/catchups.ts:760-960 (advance machinery); admin-analytics.ts structure (26 raw queries, per-view batching confirmed — one admin view fires ≤10 parallel queries, which can transiently occupy its instance's 10-conn pool; examined and accepted as admin-only transient, not reported); users/search + users-by-batch routes (take-bounded, spot-checked); schema.prisma model/index inventory. INSTALLED-SOURCE VERIFICATION: node_modules/pg-pool/index.js (max=10 line 89, min=0, idleTimeoutMillis=10000 lines 98-99, maxLifetimeSeconds=0, checkout-queues-forever lines 205-207), @prisma/adapter-pg/dist/index.js (config passthrough to pg.Pool 772-788, unnamed statements 656, per-query pool.query vs per-tx pool.connect 715-737, pool error listener 789-793), @prisma/client/runtime/client.js (itx defaults maxWait 2e3 / timeout 5e3). CONSCIOUSLY SKIPPED: feed/posts/comments action-level race analysis, R2/sharp internals, IST date math, Razorpay/Resend webhooks — other investigators' territories; I entered them only where my lens crossed (upload body cap, mail-queue connection dwell). .env could not be read (permission denied) — DATABASE_URL shape taken from AGENTS.md (port 6543, ?pgbouncer=true) and code; note that even if the URL carried connection_limit/pool params, node-pg does not parse them, so the pg defaults verified above are authoritative. THE ARITHMETIC TABLE (the lens deliverable). Facts: one pg.Pool per Vercel instance, max 10, checkout-wait unbounded; Vercel Hobby plan (stated in api/retention/sweep comment: \"Hobby plan allows two [crons]\"), Fluid compute assumed (default since 2025), region bom1 (vercel.json) = same metro as Supabase ap-south-1, RTT ~1-2ms; Supabase FREE plan (OPERATIONS.md:57) — assumption stated: Nano compute, Supavisor transaction pooler max ~200 client connections, default pool_size ~15 server connections, Postgres max_connections 60. Per authenticated pageview, statements counted from code: auth findUnique (1, cache-deduped) + notification.count (1) + advanceDueCatchups findMany (1+) + touchLastSeen (2 writes) + verificationMailState (0-1) + page queries (~3-6) + after() drain idle pass (updateMany reclaim + 2x budget count + findFirst + waiting count = 5) ≈ 13-16 statements ≈ 30-60ms total connection dwell at in-region latency; server actions that revalidatePath re-run the layout set (≈2x for interactive sessions). Load model at the 2,000-member ceiling: peak ~20-30 pageviews/s (launch burst) → 300-500 statements/s → ~1-2 concurrent connections on average. ROW 1 — client-connection cap: exhaustion needs ~20 simultaneously pool-saturated instances (20x10=200) ≈ ~200 concurrent in-flight statements ≈ at 2-3ms/stmt ~70k-100k stmt/s ≈ thousands of pageviews/s — three orders of magnitude past the ceiling; dev machine + Prisma Studio + scripts on the same shared DB add ≤~15 clients, immaterial. VERDICT: safe. ROW 2 — Supavisor server pool (15): throughput ceiling ≈ 15/mean-statement-seconds. At 3ms → ~5,000 stmt/s (~300 pageviews/s, 10x burst headroom). At 150ms (the Place altNames seq scan) → ~100 stmt/s → 15-25 concurrent typists saturate it — this is why the gazetteer scan is the High finding: slow queries, not connection counts, are the only realistic way this stack falls over at 2,000 users.
